findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting was never customized
findings.body: The migration runs `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Discourse only writes a site_settings row when a value differs from its default, so on a fresh install (or any site where the admin never changed `embed_category`) this query returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, making `[0]['id']` raise NoMethodError and the migration fail. The `if category_id == 0` fallback never gets a chance to run. The same nil-dereference pattern exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. The migration must handle empty result sets before indexing into them.

findings.title: Raw string interpolation of host values into INSERT SQL
findings.body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by interpolating each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting directly into SQL. A host value containing a single quote (a typo like `o'brien.com`) will break the SQL statement and abort the migration mid-way, and in general this is an injection vector. The values should be quoted/escaped (e.g. via `sanitize_sql_array` or `quote`) or inserted through ActiveRecord models.

findings.title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) for unknown or malformed requests
findings.body: `update` does `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then passes the result to `save_host`, which calls `host.host = ...` — if no record exists with that id, `host` is nil and the controller raises NoMethodError. `destroy` (line 15-16) has the same problem with `host.destroy`. Additionally, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking that the `:embeddable_host` key exists, so a request without that payload also 500s. These should render a 404/validation error instead.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
findings.body: The `update` action re-serializes `@embedding` without reading or persisting anything from the request body. The route (config/routes.rb line 139) exposes a PUT endpoint and the admin controller's `saveChanges` action calls `embedding.update({})`, but the server discards whatever is sent. Any client that believes it saved embedding settings gets a success response while nothing was stored. Either the action should apply and persist the submitted attributes, or the route/action and the client `saveChanges` code should be removed.

findings.title: Embed referer check now performs an uncached, unindexed DB query on every request
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` / `record_for_host` run `where("lower(host) = ?", ...)` against the database, and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` calls this on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request — these are hit on every page view of every embedding site. The previous implementation read a cached in-memory site setting. The new `embeddable_hosts` table has no index on `host` (and none is added in the migration), so each embed request is a full table scan. Add an index and/or cache the host list.

findings.title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators are in swapped files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while all the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The fabricators still register globally so tests pass, but the file organization is inverted and will confuse anyone maintaining these specs; each fabricator should live in its own named file.

findings.title: Validation permits a port but host matching never includes it, so such hosts can never work
findings.body: The format regex accepts hosts like `localhost:3000` (the `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` group), and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path — not the port. However `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which excludes the port. So an admin can save an embeddable host containing a port, it validates fine, and then every embed request from that host is rejected because `localhost:3000 != localhost`. Either strip/forbid the port or compare on host:port.

findings.title: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (e.g. created by a plugin or a partially-applied migration) without warning, destroying any rows. `force: true` is a development convenience and should not ship in a production migration. Also, the raw `execute` statements inside `change` make the migration non-reversible despite using `change`.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
findings.body: Both new controller specs (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController) only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts (including the nil-id 500 behavior), for the category_id defaulting to uncategorized, or for the embedding show/update endpoints. The migration's data conversion from the old site settings is also untested.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer tests the blank-host case
findings.body: After the refactor, this test no longer creates any embeddable host but also does not set `embed_truncate`, so the assertion `topic.expandable_first_post? == false` passes merely because `embed_truncate` is false by default — not because there is no embeddable host. The old test explicitly set `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`. Since `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults hosts at all (app/models/topic.rb line 869), the test name is misleading and the guard it claims to verify was removed; it should be renamed or updated to reflect the new condition.
